articles.title_pt: Detecting Primordial Black Holes By The Stars They Destroy
articles.excerpt: Astrophysicists wonder if primordial black holes could be part, or maybe all, of dark matter. They're theorized to have formed immediately after the Big Bang from pockets of dense matter. New research shows how they might be detected: in the bbright flash generated by the stars they consume from the inside out.
articles.summary: Astrophysicists are studying whether primordial black holes could comprise dark matter and how they might be detected through the bright flashes created when they consume stars from the inside out.

articles.title_pt: Ultra-Thin "Rainbow" Sails Could Power Spacecraft and Shade the Earth
articles.excerpt: For years, whimsically minded space enthusiasts have been dreaming of sailing across the vastness of the void on beams of sunlight. Photons, the massless particles that make up those beams of sunlight, still carry momentum, and can therefore impart a gentle push when they bounce off a surface. This force is the concept behind “solar sailing”, which has been having a bit of a moment in the last decade as several proof-of-concept flights have shown it is indeed actually feasible. Now a new paper, available in pre-print on arXiv from researchers at the Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT)…
articles.summary: Pesquisadores estudam o conceito de velas solares ultrafinas propulsionadas por fotons. A tecnologia pode servir para movimentar espaconaves e sombrear a Terra.
